74: ### Global Component Changelog
75: 
76: A global entry is written to `.skilled/changelog/{component}/v{VERSION}.md`.
77: `{component}` is a lowercase kebab-case segment matching `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, or `{hub}/{link}` when the folder is a hub, with each segment matching that pattern.

85: | `patch` | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH+1}.0` | Incremental improvement, bug fix, refactor, docs, cleanup |

99: 
100: Read `assets/changelog-template.md` before generating global content. 101: 
102: The contract in one pass:
103: 
104: 1. Frontmatter first, then an optional editorial title H1, then the summary narrative. No version header, backlink or version-date line.
105: 2. Compact under 10 reader-visible changes when the release is neither major nor breaking: summary, `## What's New at a Glance` and `## Upgrade`, with `## Why This Release` only when the summary does not say why.
106: 3. Expanded for 10 or more changes, a major bump or any breaking change: opening narrative, `## Why This Release`, `## What's New at a Glance`, topical H2 sections with benefit-led H4 items and `## Upgrade Notes`.
107: 4. A spec-folder blockquote, `> Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})`, when the release has a spec folder.
108: 5. Content chosen by reader impact and each fact said once. No file, test or schema tables unless the numbers are the story.
109: 
110: When a source such as an older command snippet conflicts with the template, follow the template, write the narrative format and record the mismatch rather than inventing a hybrid.

113: 
114: A global entry must be as findable as a spec document, so its frontmatter block carries these five keys, in this order:
115: 
116: | Key | Value |
117: | --- | --- |
118: | `title` | `<component> v<version>, <editorial title>`, or `<component> v<version>` when the entry has no editorial title. A Skilled release entry uses its H1, or `Skilled v<version>` |
119: | `description` | One or two plain sentences, 250 characters at most, saying what the release changed |
120: | `trigger_phrases` | The identity phrases first, then one or two topic phrases |
121: | `importance_tier` | `"normal"` |
122: | `contextType` | `"general"` |
123: 
124: Identity phrases name the entry the way a reader asks for it.
125: A skill entry declares `<component> v<version>` and `<component> <version>`, where `<component>` is the `name:` in the `SKILL.md` of the folder that holds the entry's changelog folder, never a `{hub}/{link}` target.
126: The deep-loop runtime has no `SKILL.md` and is `deep-loop-runtime`.
127: A Skilled release entry declares `v<version> release notes` and `skilled v<version>`.
128: A topic phrase is 2 to 6 words from the entry's own text that name what changed.
129: It carries no version number and never fits any release the way "bug fixes" would.
130: A component entry may keep a `version:` key after the five.

136: ## 6. TOPOLOGY AND TARGET RESOLUTION
137: 
138: ### Mode Detection
139: 
140: For a spec folder, read `implementation-summary.md` first and `spec.md` for the title, purpose and level. Read `tasks.md` only to confirm what shipped. Every source resolves to global mode:
141: 
142: 1. `--nested` present: stop, say packet-local changelogs are deprecated and offer a global entry.
143: 2. A spec folder, including a phase child, a phase parent or a folder that already has `changelog/`, resolves to the global component its changed paths touch (Global Component Discovery below).
144: 3. A component hint or git history source is built from recent commits and the files they touched.
145: 
146: ### Global Component Discovery
147: 
148: Discover component folders from the repository at run time with `ls -d .skilled/changelog/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort`, never from a hardcoded table. Then resolve:
149: 
150: 1. Each folder is a plain component name, such as `sk-doc` or `system-spec-kit`, with no numeric prefix. One folder is not a skill: `skilled` is the framework release line, with one entry per Skilled release.
151: 2. Match changed paths against folder names by whole path segment, never by substring.
152: 3. Match `.skilled/skills/{name}/**` to the folder named `{name}`, and `.skilled/commands/**` or `.skilled/agents/**` to the folder that owns them.
153: 4. Resolve a hub to one of its links, never to the hub folder.
154:    A hub is a real folder other than `skilled`, such as `sk-doc` or `sk-code`, holding one link per member packet plus `parent`, the hub's own changelog.
155:    `ls -l .skilled/changelog/{hub}/` lists them.
156:    A path under `.skilled/skills/{hub}/{packet}/` resolves to the link whose target is `{packet}/changelog`.
157:    Any other path under the hub, and a hint that names the hub, resolve to `{hub}/parent`.
158:    A hint that names a member by its link, its packet folder or `{hub}/{link}` resolves to that link.
159: 5. Match `component_hint` against folder names exactly.
160: 6. Use spec path segments as a tiebreaker.
161: 7. Resolve to `skilled` only when `component_hint` names it. A changed path never selects it, because the operator chooses a framework release.
162: 8. If nothing matches, do not invent or default a folder. Pause and ask which component the changelog belongs to.
163: 
164: Then choose the target:
165: 
166: 1. A component with more than 60 percent of the changed files is primary.
167: 2. With several roughly equal components, pick the primary by file count and list the rest as secondary.
168: 3. Verify the target folder exists before writing, and never create a missing one.

173: 
174: Complete these seven steps in order. The command YAMLs number the same workflow as eight steps, because they run the optional GitHub release as its own step 7.
175: 
176: Before writing, validate each authored component, packet or phase slug. Exact version filenames and frozen changelog paths stay exempt.

178: ```bash

182: 1. **Analyze context.** Resolve the source type and read the source (section 6). Compile `work_context`: what changed for the reader, the change type, the level and the source.
183: 2. **Resolve output target.** Discover the folders, match paths and hints (section 6), choose the primary component, list secondary ones and verify `.skilled/changelog/{resolved_folder}/` exists.
184: 3. **Determine version.** Do these in order:
185:    - List the `v*.md` entries in the target folder and in its generation folders (`v1+/`, `v2+/` and so on).
186:    - List the version entries on the upstream branch with `git ls-tree`, which reads the branch's upstream, else `origin/main`.
187:    - Start from the highest of the local and upstream `vX.Y.Z.B` versions, choose the bump (section 4) and calculate the next version.
188:    - Increment the build segment while the file exists locally or upstream, because two branches numbering from their own checkout pick the same version and collide at merge.
189:    - Without a reachable upstream, number locally and say so in the report.
190:    For the `skilled` release line with at least one entry, first check the highest entry for a release tag with `git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin refs/tags/v{latest}`:

192:    - A bump the operator chose is not applied, and the report says so, and says that tagging the open release first starts a new one.
193:    - When the open entry exists only upstream, stop and ask for a merge or rebase first.
194:    - Any exit other than 0 or 2 means the check failed, so number a new entry and say so rather than risk editing a release that already shipped.
195:    Every other component numbers a new entry.
196: 4. **Generate content.** Read `assets/changelog-template.md`, then:
197:    - Write the frontmatter block per the Frontmatter Contract in section 5.
198:    - Choose the content before writing it (template section 3). List what changed, keep what the reader would notice, act on or decide differently about, merge items with the same effect and drop the housekeeping.
199:    - Select compact or expanded from the changes that survive (template section 5).
200:    - Write each section to its one job, so a fact appears once: themes in the opening, the gap in Why This Release, one payoff line per theme at a glance, the detail in the H4 items and only actions in the upgrade notes.
201:    - Lead with why the release matters, and add a table only when its numbers are the story.
202:    - When extending an open release, read the entry first and fold the new work into it.
203:      Add its section or H4 items, a glance bullet in section order, its spec folder on the spec-folder line and any upgrade action.
204:      Widen the opening and Why This Release only enough to cover the new theme, keep the title unless the new work changes the headline, and correct any existing sentence the new work makes untrue.
205: 5. **Validate quality.** Run the section 9 checks on the draft. For a new entry, confirm the version is strictly greater than the latest one and no file exists at the target. For an extension, confirm the target is the open entry. Confirm every path the entry names exists. Apply the cut test (template section 3), fix what is safe and revalidate.
206: 6. **Write the file.** Write `.skilled/changelog/{primary_component}/v{next_version}.md`, or edit the open entry in place when extending, then read back its first lines.
207:    Set `next_version` in every version carrier the component's skill root already has (`SKILL.md`, `description.json`, `hub-router.json` and `mode-registry.json`), never in `README.md` or a hub `ROUTER.md`, whose versions are each document's own.
208:    For a hub, run `node .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/parent-skill-check.cjs` on the hub and stop on a non-zero exit.
209:    Report secondary components as candidates rather than writing extra files.
210: 7. **Report and preserve context.** Report the path, component, version, whether the entry is new or extended, bump type, summary, section count and files tracked. A spec-folder source can preserve context through the normal memory save workflow. Do not claim completion before the written file is verified.
211: 
212: Pause when confidence drops below 40 percent, component resolution stays ambiguous, the calculated version looks wrong or a required section would be empty.
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ## 8. NOTATION AND FORMAT RULES
217: 
218: The voice, structure, omission and length rules live in `assets/changelog-template.md` sections 3 and 4. The non-negotiables are:
219: 
220: 1. Write for a smart person who is not a developer, and lead with why the release matters.
221: 2. Keep what the reader would notice or act on. Drop file inventories, test counts, internal labels, process detail and follow-on housekeeping, and compress reverted work to one story sentence or nothing.
222: 3. Say each fact once, in the section whose job it is.
223: 4. Bold lead-in sentences on glance bullets, H4 item headings of 2-7 words (10 at most), an ` ` line before every H2 (the opening, Why This Release, What's New at a Glance and every later section), nothing between H4 items, no `---` rule in the body and inline `**Breaking:**` markers.
224: 5. No Oxford commas, em dashes or semicolons, per the Human Voice Rules.
225: 
226: ### Release Notes
227: 
228: For GitHub release notes, use the changelog content with any YAML frontmatter and the editorial title H1 removed, keeping its spacing, then append an ` ` line and the pointer:
229: 
230: ```text
231:  
232: 
233: Full changelog: `.skilled/changelog/{component}/v{VERSION}.md`
234: ```
235: 
236: The command YAMLs own the release itself, as `step_7_publish_release`.
237: They run it only when `publish_release` is explicitly true and the component is `skilled`, the framework release line.
238: Any other component skips the release, because component versions share the `vX.X.X.X` shape with release tags and a component version must never become one.
239: The tag is `v{next_version}`, and the release title is the tag followed by the entry's editorial title, the H1 without its leading version.
240: The step checks for a tag collision and an authenticated `gh`, then runs `git tag -a`, `git push origin {release_tag}` and `gh release create {release_tag} --title {release_title} --notes-file {notes_file}`, which publishes at once with no draft stage.
241: `:confirm` shows the exact commands and runs them only after approval.
242: 
243: ---
244: 
245: ## 9. VALIDATION
246: 
247: Validate the target, version and content before writing.
248: 
249: Global changelog checks:
250: 
251: 1. The target is `.skilled/changelog/{component}/v{VERSION}.md` in an existing folder, and no file exists at that path. Extending an open `skilled` release is the one exception: the target is that release's existing entry.
252: 2. The version follows `vX.Y.Z.B` and is strictly greater than the latest one in the folder, counting its generation folders. An extension keeps the open release's version.
253: 3. The frontmatter carries `title`, `description`, `trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier` and `contextType` in contract order, with both identity phrases for the target path and at least one topic phrase. `validate_document.py` blocks an entry whose block, keys or phrases are missing.
254: 4. The prose opens with the summary narrative, and the spec-folder blockquote is present when the source is a spec folder.
255: 5. The tier's sections are present: compact carries the summary, `## What's New at a Glance` and `## Upgrade`. Expanded carries the opening narrative, `## Why This Release`, `## What's New at a Glance`, at least one topical H2 with H4 items and `## Upgrade Notes`.
256: 6. No Files Changed, Test Impact or Schema Changes section. Any table passes the earned-evidence rule.
257: 7. Omission applied: no file inventories, test counts, process detail or housekeeping items. No internal labels (task, requirement, scenario or finding IDs, packet or phase numbers) appear outside the spec-folder line.
258: 8. Each fact appears once: no sentence restates one from another section, and each glance bullet adds something the summary did not.
259: 9. The template's ceilings hold: summary within 3 sentences, opening within 5 paragraphs, Why This Release within 3 short paragraphs or 4 sentences, at most 12 glance bullets, H4 items within 7 paragraphs, H4 headings within 10 words and compact files within 40 prose lines.
260: 10. H4 headings are benefit-led and never numbered or sentence-length, and no H3 sits inside a topical section.
261: 
262: Voice gate, run on the draft before writing:
263: 
264: ```bash
265: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/scripts/hvr_scan.py <draft-file>
266: ```
267: 
268: The scan must report zero hard blockers (banned punctuation or words).
269: Deductions below that threshold are acceptable.
270: If the scanner is unavailable, apply the rules by hand and record that the scan was skipped.
271: Structural checks complement it:
272: - bold lead-ins on glance bullets.
273: - an ` ` line before every H2.
274: - nothing between H4 items.
275: - no `---` rule in the body.
276: - no `**Problem:**`/`**Fix:**` labels.
277: - inline `**Breaking:**` markers.
278: 
279: Packet-local files are deprecated, so no new one is validated here. `validate_document.py` still checks the existing ones under `specs/**/changelog/`.
280: 
281: After writing, run the shared markdown checks:
282: 
283: ```bash
284: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/validate_document.py <written-file>
285: python3 .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/scripts/extract_structure.py <written-file>
286: ```
287: 
288: If validation fails, fix the blocking issues or report the exact blocker and command output.
289: 
290: ---
291: 
292: ## 10. RULES
293: 
294: ### ✅ ALWAYS
295: 
296: 1. Follow the seven-step workflow in order.
297: 2. Read `assets/changelog-template.md` before generating global content.
298: 3. Discover global component folders from `.skilled/changelog/` at run time, and resolve to an existing one before writing.
299: 4. Keep global versions four-part and strictly sequential. Extending an untagged `skilled` release keeps its version.
300: 5. Choose content by reader impact and say each fact once.
301: 6. Refuse `--nested` and route a spec-folder source to a global component entry.
302: 7. List secondary affected components.
303: 8. Verify the written file before claiming completion.
304: 9. Keep this packet self-contained, with the advisor identity at the `sk-doc` hub root.
305: 
306: ### ⛔ NEVER
307: 
308: 1. Add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.
309: 2. Overwrite an existing changelog or reuse an existing version. Extending an untagged `skilled` release entry is the one exception, and it adds to the entry rather than replacing it.
310: 3. Guess a component folder, or create a missing one.
311: 4. Write an entry with an empty summary or an empty required section.
312: 5. Write a new packet-local changelog, or use the deprecated nested generator to create one. Its `--write` only re-renders an existing packet changelog.
313: 6. Make the command router or YAML the only workflow contract.
314: 7. Hide a source-format conflict. Record it and follow the template.
315: 
316: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
317: 
318: 1. No source context can be found in a spec folder, component history or git history.
319: 2. Component resolution stays ambiguous after file-count and path-segment analysis.
320: 3. The calculated version is unexpected or cannot be made unique.
321: 4. A required section would be empty.
322: 5. The user asks for a GitHub release with no git release workflow or command context available.
323: 6. Validation still fails after safe local fixes.
324: 
325: ---
326: 
327: ## 11. REFERENCES
328: 
329: 1. `assets/changelog-template.md`: the canonical format, selection, voice and length rules.
330: 2. `references/README.md`: the route map to `worked-examples.md` (filled-in entries), `version-bump-rules.md` (concrete version choices) and `topology-edge-cases.md` (placement, back-dating, source conflicts and the release flow).
331: 3. `.skilled/commands/create/changelog.md`: the thin `/create:changelog` router.
332: 4. `.skilled/commands/create/assets/create-changelog-auto.yaml` and `create-changelog-confirm.yaml`: the `:auto` and `:confirm` workflows, which resolve to this same contract.
333: 
334: ---
335: 
336: ## 12. SUCCESS CRITERIA
337: 
338: The workflow succeeds when:
339: 
340: 1. The file lands at its global component path, and a `--nested` request is refused with a global entry offered instead.
341: 2. Global versioning is sequential, unique and four-part, and an untagged `skilled` release is extended rather than followed by a second untagged entry.
342: 3. The entry follows the template's compact or expanded shape and reads in the v4 style: why first, benefit-led headings, only what the reader needs and each fact said once.
343: 4. A release body, when requested, uses the entry and appends the full changelog path.
344: 5. Validation passes, or the remaining issue is escalated with exact evidence.
345: 6. No other file changes unless the user asked for it.

74: ### Global Component Changelog

76: A global entry is written to `.skilled/changelog/{component}/v{VERSION}.md`.

82: | --- | --- | --- |
83: | `major` | `{MAJOR+1}.0.0.0` | Breaking, overhaul, rewrite, migration, platform version jump |
84: | `minor` | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR+1}.0.0` | Significant new feature or subsystem addition |
85: | `patch` | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH+1}.0` | Incremental improvement, bug fix, refactor, docs, cleanup |

104: 1. Frontmatter first, then an optional editorial title H1, then the summary narrative. No version header, backlink or version-date line.

119: | `description` | One or two plain sentences, 250 characters at most, saying what the release changed |
120: | `trigger_phrases` | The identity phrases first, then one or two topic phrases |
121: | `importance_tier` | `"normal"` |
122: | `contextType` | `"general"` |

126: The deep-loop runtime has no `SKILL.md` and is `deep-loop-runtime`.
127: A Skilled release entry declares `v<version> release notes` and `skilled v<version>`.
128: A topic phrase is 2 to 6 words from the entry's own text that name what changed.
129: It carries no version number and never fits any release the way "bug fixes" would.
130: A component entry may keep a `version:` key after the five.

132: Existing packet-local entries keep the block the deprecated nested generator renders, with an identity phrase derived from the output path.

141: 
142: 1. `--nested` present: stop, say packet-local changelogs are deprecated and offer a global entry.

149: 
150: 1. Each folder is a plain component name, such as `sk-doc` or `system-spec-kit`, with no numeric prefix. One folder is not a skill: `skilled` is the framework release line, with one entry per Skilled release.
151: 2. Match changed paths against folder names by whole path segment, never by substring.
152: 3. Match `.skilled/skills/{name}/**` to the folder named `{name}`, and `.skilled/commands/**` or `.skilled/agents/**` to the folder that owns them.
153: 4. Resolve a hub to one of its links, never to the hub folder.
154:    A hub is a real folder other than `skilled`, such as `sk-doc` or `sk-code`, holding one link per member packet plus `parent`, the hub's own changelog.

167: 2. With several roughly equal components, pick the primary by file count and list the rest as secondary.

220: 1. Write for a smart person who is not a developer, and lead with why the release matters.

63: from pathlib import Path
64: 
65: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
66: RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
67: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/README.md"

72:     # Deprecated: kept so a packet-local request that lands here is refused and offered a global entry.
73:     "packet_local": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["packet-local changelog", "nested changelog", "--nested"]},
74: }

77:     "Confirm the global component the change belongs to",
78:     "Confirm the four-part version and whether --bump/--release applies",
79: ]
80: 
81: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
82:     docs = []
83:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
84:         if base.exists():
85:             docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
86:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}
87: 
88: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
89:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
90:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
91:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
92:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
93:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
94: 
95: def load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:
96:     guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
97:     if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:
98:         load(guarded)
99:         loaded.append(guarded)
100:         seen.add(guarded)
101: 
102: def score_intents(request) -> dict:
103:     text = request.text.lower()
104:     scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}
105:     for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():
106:         for kw in cfg["keywords"]:
107:             if kw in text:
108:                 scores[intent] += cfg["weight"]
109:     return scores
110:

112:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
113:     loaded, seen = [], set()
114:     scores = score_intents(request)
115: 
116:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: unclear source/mode
117:         load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)
118:         return {
119:             "load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK",
120:             "needs_disambiguation": True,
121:             "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,
122:             "resources": loaded,
123:         }

125:     output_mode = max(scores, key=scores.get)                # Tier 2: pick the intent
126:     if output_mode == "packet_local":                        # Deprecated: refuse and write nothing
127:         return {
128:             "output_mode": "refused",
129:             "writes": [],
130:             "message": "Packet-local changelogs are deprecated. Spec folders no longer get changelogs.",
131:             "offer": "Write a global component entry under .skilled/changelog/ instead (section 4)",
132:         }

135:     for path in sorted(inventory):
136:         load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)

38: ## 3. MACHINE ROUTER
39:

41: reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.

45: ### Family Boundary
46: 
47: This is a nested workflow packet under `sk-doc` and owns changelog authoring only. The single advisor identity lives at the `sk-doc` hub root, so never add a packet-local `graph-metadata.json`.

49: ### Router Resilience
50: 
51: The packet has one output mode, the global component entry (section 6). The advisor does not guarantee that a packet-local request lands here. When one does, the router refuses it as deprecated and offers a global entry. Its references are flat, so it uses no `references/<key>/` discovery.
52: 
53: - Load an optional resource only after resolving it under this packet and confirming it exists.
54: - Treat `references/README.md` as the fallback route map when the topology or output mode is unclear.
55: - Ask for the missing source type, target or version intent instead of silently loading nothing.
56: - Add a `references/<key>/` runtime-key router only if the packet gains keyed subdirectories.
57: 
58: ### Smart Router Pseudocode
59: 
60: The resilient router discovers resources at call time, loads only what exists, scores the global intent against the deprecated packet-local one, refuses a packet-local request without writing and returns a disambiguation checklist rather than loading nothing:
61: 
62: ```python
63: from pathlib import Path
64: 
65: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
66: RESOURCE_BASES = (SKILL_ROOT / "references", SKILL_ROOT / "assets")
67: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/README.md"
68: 
69: # Two intents, one output mode. Keywords come from this packet's activation triggers.
70: INTENT_MODEL = {
71:     "global_component": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["global changelog", "release notes", "component", "--release", "--bump"]},
72:     # Deprecated: kept so a packet-local request that lands here is refused and offered a global entry.
73:     "packet_local": {"weight": 4, "keywords": ["packet-local changelog", "nested changelog", "--nested"]},
74: }
75: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
76:     "Confirm the change source (component hint, git history, or spec folder)",
77:     "Confirm the global component the change belongs to",
78:     "Confirm the four-part version and whether --bump/--release applies",
79: ]
80: 
81: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
82:     docs = []
83:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
84:         if base.exists():
85:             docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
86:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}
87: 
88: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
89:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
90:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
91:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
92:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
93:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
94: 
95: def load_if_available(relative_path, inventory, loaded, seen) -> None:
96:     guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
97:     if guarded in inventory and guarded not in seen:
98:         load(guarded)
99:         loaded.append(guarded)
100:         seen.add(guarded)
101: 
102: def score_intents(request) -> dict:
103:     text = request.text.lower()
104:     scores = {intent: 0 for intent in INTENT_MODEL}
105:     for intent, cfg in INTENT_MODEL.items():
106:         for kw in cfg["keywords"]:
107:             if kw in text:
108:                 scores[intent] += cfg["weight"]
109:     return scores
110: 
111: def route_changelog_request(request):
112:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
113:     loaded, seen = [], set()
114:     scores = score_intents(request)
115: 
116:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 4:                      # Tier 1: unclear source/mode
117:         load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE, inventory, loaded, seen)
118:         return {
119:             "load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK",
120:             "needs_disambiguation": True,
121:             "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,
122:             "resources": loaded,
123:         }
124: 
125:     output_mode = max(scores, key=scores.get)                # Tier 2: pick the intent
126:     if output_mode == "packet_local":                        # Deprecated: refuse and write nothing
127:         return {
128:             "output_mode": "refused",
129:             "writes": [],
130:             "message": "Packet-local changelogs are deprecated. Spec folders no longer get changelogs.",
131:             "offer": "Write a global component entry under .skilled/changelog/ instead (section 4)",
132:         }
133:     # Flat resource topology: no references/<key>/ subdirectories. The mode selects the
134:     # generator target documented above, not a keyed subtree; load the flat refs that exist.
135:     for path in sorted(inventory):
136:         load_if_available(path, inventory, loaded, seen)
137:     return {"output_mode": output_mode, "resources": loaded}
138: ```

17: Concrete four-part version choices and edge distinctions for global component changelogs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Version bumps apply only to global component changelogs. Packet-local nested changelogs are deprecated, and the existing ones were never versioned this way. This file adds examples to the bump table and auto-detection order in [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) section 4, which stay authoritative.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. BUMP DECISION TABLE
28: 
29: | Bump | Calculation | Use When | Concrete Example |
30: |---|---|---|---|
31: | Major | `{MAJOR+1}.0.0.0` | Breaking change, overhaul, rewrite, migration or platform-level version shift | `v1.8.1.0` to `v2.0.0.0` for a breaking command contract rewrite |
32: | Minor | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR+1}.0.0` | Significant new feature or subsystem addition | `v1.8.1.0` to `v1.9.0.0` for a new `create-changelog` packet |
33: | Patch | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH+1}.0` | Bug fix, refactor, docs update, improvement or cleanup | `v1.8.1.0` to `v1.8.2.0` for fixing packet validation wording |
34: | Build | `{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}.{BUILD+1}` | Hotfix, typo or same-day correction on a published version | `v1.8.1.0` to `v1.8.1.1` for a release-note typo fix |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 3. MAJOR MEANS BREAKING, NOT LARGE
39: 
40: The most common mistake is choosing major because the work was large. Major means a breaking or architectural change, not high effort. Use minor for new feature work and patch for incremental repair, however many files moved.
41: 
42: ---
43: 
44: ## 4. REAL RELEASE SHAPES
45: 
46: The sk-doc entries under `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/changelog/` show normal releases. `v1.8.0.0` is a minor release that added the four-part frontmatter version standard. `v1.8.1.0` is a patch that enforces the skill-authoring contract end to end.
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 5. FIRST-ENTRY CASE
51: 
52: A global component folder that exists but holds no versions starts at `v1.0.0.0`. The workflow never creates the folder itself. If the calculated file already exists, increment `BUILD` until the filename is unique rather than overwriting.
53: 
54: The `skilled` release line has one exception. When its latest entry has no `v{latest}` tag on origin (`git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin refs/tags/v{latest}` exits 2), that release is still open. The run keeps its version, does not apply the chosen bump and says so, and folds the new work into the existing entry. Any exit other than 0 or 2 means the check failed, and the run numbers a new entry and says so.
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 6. RELATED

61: - [worked-examples.md](worked-examples.md) - filled-in global entries
62: - [topology-edge-cases.md](topology-edge-cases.md) - placement, back-dating, source conflicts and release edge cases

16: 
17: Where a changelog goes, and the edge cases around placement, back-dating, source-format conflicts and the optional release.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Mode detection and component resolution are authoritative in [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) section 6. This file carries the placement table and the edge cases around it.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. OUTPUT-MODE PLACEMENT
28: 
29: Every new entry is global. The packet-local rows record where existing files sit, and no workflow writes a new one.
30: 
31: | Output Mode | Where It Writes | Versioned? | Use For |
32: |---|---|---|---|
33: | Global component changelog | `.skilled/changelog/{component}/v{VERSION}.md` | Yes | Public component release notes |
34: | Packet-local root changelog (deprecated) | `{spec-folder}/changelog/changelog-<packet>-root.md` | No | Existing files only. `--nested` is refused |
35: | Packet-local phase changelog (deprecated) | `{phase-parent}/changelog/changelog-<packet>-<phase-folder>.md` | No | Existing files only. `--nested` is refused |
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 3. HUB VERSUS PACKET PLACEMENT
40: 
41: A changelog for the users of a component goes global. Spec packets no longer get their own changelog, so a packet's completed work, a phase child included, goes into the global entry for the component it touched. The folders under `.skilled/changelog/` are plain component names, except `skilled`, the framework release line, which the workflow writes to only when the operator names it. For ties between components, or no match at all, follow the selection rules in SKILL.md section 6 rather than guessing a folder.
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ## 4. BACK-DATING
46: 
47: The workflow sets `DATE` to today in `YYYY-MM-DD` format and defines no back-dating rule. Treat back-dating as UNKNOWN unless the user gives an explicit release-management instruction.
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 5. SOURCE CONFLICTS TO WATCH
52: 
53: The template and the command YAMLs share the v4 narrative contract. If a source still shows an older snippet (an H1 version header, a backlink, a version-date header, `###` highlight headings or Problem/Fix labels), follow `assets/changelog-template.md` and record the mismatch rather than inventing a hybrid.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 6. OPTIONAL GITHUB RELEASE FLOW
58: 
59: SKILL.md section 8 describes the release step: `skilled` only, tag `v{next_version}`, `git tag -a`, `git push origin {release_tag}` and `gh release create` with no draft stage. What the command surface adds:
60: 
61: - `publish_release` defaults to `false` in auto setup.
62: - The startup prompt asks whether to create a tag and GitHub release when `--release` is not supplied.
63: - The result reports `Release Published: yes/no/not requested`.
64: - `:confirm` shows the exact commands and runs them only after approval.
65: - `:auto` runs them when `publish_release` is true and warns when the changelog file is not yet committed, because the tag points at the current HEAD.
66: 
67: Use `--release` only after the changelog path, component and version are resolved.

15: # Changelog & Release Notes Templates - Format Reference
16: 
17: Two narrative formats for global component changelogs and their GitHub release notes. Every rule below serves one goal: the reader learns what changed for them and why, in the fewest words that still carry the connection.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### The Canonical Exemplar
22: 
23: `.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.0.0.md` is the house style, so read it before writing. It shows the opening narrative, Why This Release, What's New at a Glance, topical H2 sections with benefit-led H4 items, inline Breaking markers and Upgrade Notes. Copy its voice and shape, not its length: it records a major release, and most releases need a fraction of it. Older entries in the same folders predate this style, so do not copy them. When this template and the exemplar disagree on shape, the exemplar wins and the discrepancy is recorded.
24: 
25: ### Usage
26: 
27: The `/create:changelog` workflow reads this template at step 4. Section 5 picks the format. Packet-local changelogs are deprecated and no longer written (section 7).
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. THE TWO TIERS
32: 
33: Every entry opens with the frontmatter block that SKILL.md section 5 defines. An editorial title H1 may follow it, and then the prose starts with the summary narrative. The retired machine header (a bare version title, a backlink, a version-date line) stays gone.
34: 
35: ### Compact Format (under 10 changes, non-breaking)
36: 
37: ```markdown
38: ---
39: title: "{component} v{VERSION}"
40: description: "{What the release changed, in one or two plain sentences of 250 characters at most.}"
41: trigger_phrases:
42:   - "{component} v{VERSION}"
43:   - "{component} {VERSION}"
44:   - "{Topic phrase: 2-6 words from this entry that name what changed}"
45: importance_tier: "normal"
46: contextType: "general"
47: ---
48: 
49: {Summary: 1-3 sentences on what the release does for the reader and why it matters.}
50: 
51: > Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})
52: 
53:  
54: 
55: ## What's New at a Glance
56: 
57: - **{The change, as a short sentence.}** {One plain sentence that adds what the bold one does not say.}
58: 
59:  
60: 
61: ## Upgrade
62: 
63: {The action the reader must take, or "No migration required."}
64: ```
65: 
66: Include the spec-folder line only when the release has a spec folder. Add a `## Why This Release` section of 2-4 sentences after the summary only when the summary does not already say why, with an ` ` line before it like every other H2.
67: 
68: ### Expanded Format (10+ changes, major or breaking)
69: 
70: ```markdown
71: {The same frontmatter block as the compact format.}
72: 
73: {Opening narrative: 1-5 paragraphs in plain prose, one per theme, no headers.}
74: 
75: > Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})
76: 
77:  
78: 
79: ## Why This Release
80: 
81: {Why the release exists: the gap it closes or the gain it buys, in one to three short paragraphs or bold lead-in gain bullets.}
82: 
83:  
84: 
85: ## What's New at a Glance
86: 
87: - **{The theme, as a short sentence.}** {One plain sentence that adds what the bold one does not say.}
88: 
89:  
90: 
91: ## {Topical Domain}
92: 
93: {Optional 1-2 sentence introduction.}
94: 
95: #### {Benefit-led heading, usually 2-7 words}
96: 
97: {One or two paragraphs for most items, seven at most: what was broken, what changed and why it matters. Start where the glance bullet stopped.}
98: 
99: #### {Next heading}
100: 
101: **Breaking:** {What breaks and exactly what to do about it.}
102: 
103:  
104: 
105: ## Upgrade Notes
106: 
107: - **Adopt.** {Renames and new things to start using.}
108: - **Repoint.** {Moved paths and surfaces that changed address.}
109: - **Drop.** {Removed things and what replaces them.}
110: ```
111: 
112: Include the spec-folder line only when the release has a spec folder.
113: 
114: **Field guidelines**:
115: 
116: - **`{Topical Domain}` (H2).** Name the section for the domain it changes, the way the exemplar names `Spec Kit` and `Safer Git`, never for a change type such as `New Features` or `Bug Fixes`. Most releases need one to five domains. A release the exemplar's size may need more when each one earns its section.
117: - **`{Benefit-led heading}` (H4).** 2-7 words for most headings and 10 at most, stating the gain or the fact. Good: `Specs Move to the Top Level`. Bad: `Improved validation logic`, a numbered item or a sentence-length title.
118: - **Separators.** An ` ` line, a forced blank line, goes before every H2: between the opening and Why This Release, between Why This Release and What's New at a Glance, and between every later section. Nothing separates the H4 items inside one H2, and no `---` rule appears anywhere in the entry body.
119: - **Upgrade Notes.** Use the Adopt, Repoint and Drop lead-ins only when the release has all three kinds of work. Otherwise write plain bullets or a short paragraph, and "No upgrade needed." when there is nothing to do.
120: 
121: ---
122: 
123: ## 3. WHAT TO LEAVE OUT
124: 
125: What goes in decides the length more than the wording does, so choose the content before writing any of it. Every item dropped stays findable in the spec packet.
126: 
127: ### Choose by Reader Impact
128: 
129: List every change the source records. Keep an item only when the reader would notice it, act on it or decide differently because of it. Merge items that have the same effect for the reader, and lead with the one that matters most. A task list is evidence of what shipped, not an outline: ten tasks that produced one visible change make one bullet.
130: 
131: ### Keep
132: 
133: - User-visible behavior changes, stated as before and after.
134: - Breaking changes and the exact migration step.
135: - Anything the reader must do, adopt, repoint or stop using.
136: - Honest corrections of a claim a previous release got wrong.
137: - Numbers that are the claim itself, such as a measured cost or a limit the reader must stay under.
138: 
139: ### Drop by Default
140: 
141: - File inventories and Files Changed tables.
142: - Test counts, test tables and new test or playbook scenarios.
143: - Schema internals, index churn and machinery names the reader never touches.
144: - Internal labels such as task or requirement IDs, scenario IDs and packet or phase numbers. The spec-folder line is the one pointer an entry needs.
145: - How the work was done: review rounds, models, agents and research phases, unless it changes how far the reader can trust the result.
146: - Follow-on housekeeping: docs brought in line with the change, regenerated copies, rebuilt indexes and refreshed metadata or versions.
147: - Small fixes with no visible effect. Fold several into one sentence, or leave them out.
148: - Work tried and reverted during the cycle. It gets one story sentence at most, written into the narrative: what was tried and that it left before release. The exemplar's model is "An alignment mode was built during the cycle and removed before release, and the removal took `/deep:command-benchmark` and the conformance benchmark family with it."
149: 
150: ### Say Each Fact Once
151: 
152: Each section has one job, and a fact lives in the section whose job it is.
153: 
154: | Section | Its job | Not its job |
155: |---|---|---|
156: | Summary or opening | What the release does, told at the level of themes | Fix-by-fix detail and the numbers behind it |
157: | Why This Release | The gap the release closes or the gain it buys | The list of changes, which the glance section carries |
158: | What's New at a Glance | One line per theme, stating the payoff | The full mechanism or a sentence that restates the bold one |
159: | Topical H4 items | The detail: before, mechanism and after | The glance bullet's sentence, said again |
160: | Upgrade Notes | The actions, one line each | Why the change was made |
161: 
162: When a sentence would repeat an earlier one, cut it or replace it with something the reader does not know yet. In a compact entry, each glance bullet must add something the summary did not say.
163: 
164: ### When a Table Earns Its Place
165: 
166: A table appears only when the numbers are the claim. The exemplar carries one in six hundred lines, the measured cached-input cost per model, because the dollar difference was the finding. A table that restates prose, lists files or counts tests does not earn its place, and most entries carry none.
167: 
168: ### The Cut Test
169: 
170: Before writing the file, ask of each sentence whether the reader would miss it. Cut the ones they would not. Then check the joints: concise is not compressed, so keep the "because" and the before-and-after that make a change make sense, and restore the noun when a cut leaves a "this" with nothing to point at.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 4. WRITING STYLE RULES
175: 
176: These rules apply to changelog files and GitHub release notes. The Human Voice Rules are the authority on banned patterns, and the validator enforces both.
177: 
178: ### Voice
179: 
180: - Write for a smart person who is not a developer.
181: - Lead with why the release matters, never with technical stats.
182: - Explain each change as what was broken, what changed and why it matters.
183: - One idea per sentence, active voice, no hedging.
184: - Define a technical term on first use, such as "BM25 (exact word matching)".
185: - Name an identifier (a skill, a path or a command) only where the reader acts on it, the way the exemplar names `mode-registry.json` where it explains dispatch.
186: - No Oxford commas, em dashes or semicolons, per `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md`.
187: 
188: ### Structure
189: 
190: - Bold lead-in bullets for lists of gains or upgrade steps.
191: - H4 (`####`) for item headings, never H3. No `**Problem:**` or `**Fix:**` labels.
192: - Inline `**Breaking:**` markers where the break is described, not a separate section.
193: - No metrics soup: never pack many numbers into one sentence.
194: 
195: ### Length
196: 
197: | Element | Usually | Ceiling |
198: |---|---|---|
199: | Summary paragraph | 1-2 sentences | 3 sentences |
200: | Expanded opening narrative | 1-3 paragraphs | 5 paragraphs |

15: # Changelog & Release Notes Templates - Format Reference
16: 
17: Two narrative formats for global component changelogs and their GitHub release notes. Every rule below serves one goal: the reader learns what changed for them and why, in the fewest words that still carry the connection.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### The Canonical Exemplar
22: 
23: `.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.0.0.0.md` is the house style, so read it before writing. It shows the opening narrative, Why This Release, What's New at a Glance, topical H2 sections with benefit-led H4 items, inline Breaking markers and Upgrade Notes. Copy its voice and shape, not its length: it records a major release, and most releases need a fraction of it. Older entries in the same folders predate this style, so do not copy them. When this template and the exemplar disagree on shape, the exemplar wins and the discrepancy is recorded.
24: 
25: ### Usage
26: 
27: The `/create:changelog` workflow reads this template at step 4. Section 5 picks the format. Packet-local changelogs are deprecated and no longer written (section 7).
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. THE TWO TIERS
32: 
33: Every entry opens with the frontmatter block that SKILL.md section 5 defines. An editorial title H1 may follow it, and then the prose starts with the summary narrative. The retired machine header (a bare version title, a backlink, a version-date line) stays gone.
34: 
35: ### Compact Format (under 10 changes, non-breaking)
36: 
37: ```markdown
38: ---
39: title: "{component} v{VERSION}"
40: description: "{What the release changed, in one or two plain sentences of 250 characters at most.}"
41: trigger_phrases:
42:   - "{component} v{VERSION}"
43:   - "{component} {VERSION}"
44:   - "{Topic phrase: 2-6 words from this entry that name what changed}"
45: importance_tier: "normal"
46: contextType: "general"
47: ---
48: 
49: {Summary: 1-3 sentences on what the release does for the reader and why it matters.}
50: 
51: > Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})
52: 
53:  
54: 
55: ## What's New at a Glance
56: 
57: - **{The change, as a short sentence.}** {One plain sentence that adds what the bold one does not say.}
58: 
59:  
60: 
61: ## Upgrade
62: 
63: {The action the reader must take, or "No migration required."}
64: ```
65: 
66: Include the spec-folder line only when the release has a spec folder. Add a `## Why This Release` section of 2-4 sentences after the summary only when the summary does not already say why, with an ` ` line before it like every other H2.
67: 
68: ### Expanded Format (10+ changes, major or breaking)
69: 
70: ```markdown
71: {The same frontmatter block as the compact format.}
72: 
73: {Opening narrative: 1-5 paragraphs in plain prose, one per theme, no headers.}
74: 
75: > Spec folder: `{path}` (Level {N})
76: 
77:  
78: 
79: ## Why This Release
80: 
81: {Why the release exists: the gap it closes or the gain it buys, in one to three short paragraphs or bold lead-in gain bullets.}
82: 
83:  
84: 
85: ## What's New at a Glance
86: 
87: - **{The theme, as a short sentence.}** {One plain sentence that adds what the bold one does not say.}
88: 
89:  
90: 
91: ## {Topical Domain}
92: 
93: {Optional 1-2 sentence introduction.}
94: 
95: #### {Benefit-led heading, usually 2-7 words}
96: 
97: {One or two paragraphs for most items, seven at most: what was broken, what changed and why it matters. Start where the glance bullet stopped.}
98: 
99: #### {Next heading}
100: 
101: **Breaking:** {What breaks and exactly what to do about it.}
102: 
103:  
104: 
105: ## Upgrade Notes
106: 
107: - **Adopt.** {Renames and new things to start using.}
108: - **Repoint.** {Moved paths and surfaces that changed address.}
109: - **Drop.** {Removed things and what replaces them.}
110: ```
111: 
112: Include the spec-folder line only when the release has a spec folder.
113: 
114: **Field guidelines**:
115: 
116: - **`{Topical Domain}` (H2).** Name the section for the domain it changes, the way the exemplar names `Spec Kit` and `Safer Git`, never for a change type such as `New Features` or `Bug Fixes`. Most releases need one to five domains. A release the exemplar's size may need more when each one earns its section.
117: - **`{Benefit-led heading}` (H4).** 2-7 words for most headings and 10 at most, stating the gain or the fact. Good: `Specs Move to the Top Level`. Bad: `Improved validation logic`, a numbered item or a sentence-length title.
118: - **Separators.** An ` ` line, a forced blank line, goes before every H2: between the opening and Why This Release, between Why This Release and What's New at a Glance, and between every later section. Nothing separates the H4 items inside one H2, and no `---` rule appears anywhere in the entry body.
119: - **Upgrade Notes.** Use the Adopt, Repoint and Drop lead-ins only when the release has all three kinds of work. Otherwise write plain bullets or a short paragraph, and "No upgrade needed." when there is nothing to do.
120: 
121: ---
122: 
123: ## 3. WHAT TO LEAVE OUT
124: 
125: What goes in decides the length more than the wording does, so choose the content before writing any of it. Every item dropped stays findable in the spec packet.
126: 
127: ### Choose by Reader Impact
128: 
129: List every change the source records. Keep an item only when the reader would notice it, act on it or decide differently because of it. Merge items that have the same effect for the reader, and lead with the one that matters most. A task list is evidence of what shipped, not an outline: ten tasks that produced one visible change make one bullet.
130: 
131: ### Keep
132: 
133: - User-visible behavior changes, stated as before and after.
134: - Breaking changes and the exact migration step.
135: - Anything the reader must do, adopt, repoint or stop using.
136: - Honest corrections of a claim a previous release got wrong.
137: - Numbers that are the claim itself, such as a measured cost or a limit the reader must stay under.
138: 
139: ### Drop by Default
140: 
141: - File inventories and Files Changed tables.
142: - Test counts, test tables and new test or playbook scenarios.
143: - Schema internals, index churn and machinery names the reader never touches.
144: - Internal labels such as task or requirement IDs, scenario IDs and packet or phase numbers. The spec-folder line is the one pointer an entry needs.
145: - How the work was done: review rounds, models, agents and research phases, unless it changes how far the reader can trust the result.
146: - Follow-on housekeeping: docs brought in line with the change, regenerated copies, rebuilt indexes and refreshed metadata or versions.
147: - Small fixes with no visible effect. Fold several into one sentence, or leave them out.
148: - Work tried and reverted during the cycle. It gets one story sentence at most, written into the narrative: what was tried and that it left before release. The exemplar's model is "An alignment mode was built during the cycle and removed before release, and the removal took `/deep:command-benchmark` and the conformance benchmark family with it."
149: 
150: ### Say Each Fact Once
151: 
152: Each section has one job, and a fact lives in the section whose job it is.
153: 
154: | Section | Its job | Not its job |
155: |---|---|---|
156: | Summary or opening | What the release does, told at the level of themes | Fix-by-fix detail and the numbers behind it |
157: | Why This Release | The gap the release closes or the gain it buys | The list of changes, which the glance section carries |
158: | What's New at a Glance | One line per theme, stating the payoff | The full mechanism or a sentence that restates the bold one |
159: | Topical H4 items | The detail: before, mechanism and after | The glance bullet's sentence, said again |
160: | Upgrade Notes | The actions, one line each | Why the change was made |
161: 
162: When a sentence would repeat an earlier one, cut it or replace it with something the reader does not know yet. In a compact entry, each glance bullet must add something the summary did not say.
163: 
164: ### When a Table Earns Its Place
165: 
166: A table appears only when the numbers are the claim. The exemplar carries one in six hundred lines, the measured cached-input cost per model, because the dollar difference was the finding. A table that restates prose, lists files or counts tests does not earn its place, and most entries carry none.
167: 
168: ### The Cut Test
169: 
170: Before writing the file, ask of each sentence whether the reader would miss it. Cut the ones they would not. Then check the joints: concise is not compressed, so keep the "because" and the before-and-after that make a change make sense, and restore the noun when a cut leaves a "this" with nothing to point at.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 4. WRITING STYLE RULES
175: 
176: These rules apply to changelog files and GitHub release notes. The Human Voice Rules are the authority on banned patterns, and the validator enforces both.
177: 
178: ### Voice
179: 
180: - Write for a smart person who is not a developer.
181: - Lead with why the release matters, never with technical stats.
182: - Explain each change as what was broken, what changed and why it matters.
183: - One idea per sentence, active voice, no hedging.
184: - Define a technical term on first use, such as "BM25 (exact word matching)".
185: - Name an identifier (a skill, a path or a command) only where the reader acts on it, the way the exemplar names `mode-registry.json` where it explains dispatch.
186: - No Oxford commas, em dashes or semicolons, per `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md`.
187: 
188: ### Structure
189: 
190: - Bold lead-in bullets for lists of gains or upgrade steps.
191: - H4 (`####`) for item headings, never H3. No `**Problem:**` or `**Fix:**` labels.
192: - Inline `**Breaking:**` markers where the break is described, not a separate section.
193: - No metrics soup: never pack many numbers into one sentence.
194: 
195: ### Length
196: 
197: | Element | Usually | Ceiling |
198: |---|---|---|
199: | Summary paragraph | 1-2 sentences | 3 sentences |
200: | Expanded opening narrative | 1-3 paragraphs | 5 paragraphs |
201: | Why This Release | 1-2 short paragraphs | 3 short paragraphs or 4 sentences, gain bullets allowed |
202: | What's New at a Glance | 3-6 bullets compact, 5-9 expanded | 12 bullets, one line each |
203: | Glance bullet | A bold sentence and one plain sentence | A bold sentence and three plain sentences |
204: | H4 item narrative | 1-2 paragraphs | 7 paragraphs |
205: | H4 heading | 2-7 words | 10 words |
206: | Compact file total | 10-25 lines of prose | 40 lines of prose |
207: 
208: Validation checks the ceilings, and each one sits at or above what the exemplar does, so the exemplar passes every check it teaches. The usual column is the target. A release with one fix reads short.
209: 
210: ---
211:

213: 
214: | Release Type | Format | When to Use |
215: |---|---|---|
216: | Hotfix (1-3 changes) | Compact | Quick bug fix, typo correction |
217: | Feature release (4-9 changes) | Compact | New feature, small refactor |
218: | Major release (10+ changes) | Expanded | Overhaul, multi-part work |
219: | Breaking change | Expanded | Any release requiring migration, regardless of count |
220: 
221: Count the changes that survive section 3, not the tasks behind them.
222: 
223: ```text
224: Count the changes in the release.
225: ├─> < 10 changes AND not major AND not breaking  → Compact format
226: ├─> >= 10 changes OR major bump                  → Expanded format
227: └─> Any breaking change                          → Expanded format
228: ```

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.

19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |

37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073: 
1074: ---
